PR_H124.outlook_verbatim: Exosens is fully on track to deliver its 2024 guidance communicated at IPO, notably expecting: High-teens organic revenue growth and around 30% total revenue growth including 2024 acquisitions. Adjusted EBITDA of at least €115 million (excluding 2024 acquisitions) and adjusted EBITDA margin slightly above the 2023 level. Adjusted EBIT margin between 24-25%, with an organic cash conversion rate of 75-80%. Net leverage around 1.6x by year-end, including recent and planned acquisitions.
PR_H124.like_for_like_definition: Organic growth for the half-year ended 30 June 2024 therefore excludes the contribution of ProxiVision, El-Mul and Telops, acquired by the Group in June 2023, July 2023 and October 2023, respectively.
PR_H124.events: Centronics acquisition closed 31 July 2024; LR Tech acquisition completed 1 September 2024; EcoVadis Silver Medal August 2024.

PR_9M24.outlook_verbatim: Taking account of the strong performance achieved in the first nine months of the year, Exosens is fully on track to deliver on its 2024 guidance communicated as part of its IPO, notably expecting: High-teens organic revenue growth and around 30% total revenue growth including 2024 acquisitions; Adjusted EBITDA of at least €115 million (excluding 2024 acquisitions) and adjusted EBITDA margin slightly above the 2023 level; Adjusted EBIT margin between 24-25%, with a cash conversion rate of 75-80%; Net leverage around 1.6x by year-end, including recent and planned acquisitions.
PR_9M24.like_for_like_definition: Organic growth for the nine-month period ended 30 September 2024 therefore excludes the contribution of Telops, El-Mul, and Photonis Germany (formerly ProxiVision), acquired by the Group in October 2023, July 2023, and June 2023, respectively.
orders_and_events: On 22 October 2024, Exosens announced the signing of a definitive agreement to acquire NVLS, a specialist developer and manufacturer of man-portable night vision and thermal devices, based in Spain with 63 employees.

This marks the third bolt-on acquisition announced by the Group since the beginning of the year, after LR Tech and Centronic, acquired in September 2024 and July 2024, respectively. On a combined basis, these three companies generated total revenue of €26 million in their last reported fiscal year (in local GAAP accounting standards).

PR_FY24.outlook_verbatim: Exosens expects a continued strong performance in 2025, with revenue growth in the high-teens and adjusted EBITDA growth in the low twenties compared to 2024. The Group expects a high-teens 2024-2026 adjusted EBITDA CAGR and a cash conversion ratio in the range of 70%-75% over the period, taking into account capacity investment in Europe and in the US. Furthermore, the Group intends to pursue its growth strategy, at a pace consistent with historical trend, while maintaining a leverage ratio of around 2x.
PR_FY24.capacity_plan_verbatim: In order to meet this demand Exosens decided to invest €20m to expand its production capacity not only in Europe but also in the US with, for the first time, a new production plant in the US, which will give us additional market opportunities.
PR_FY24.like_for_like_definition: Like-for-like growth for the fiscal year ended 31 December 2024 therefore excludes the contribution of Telops, El-Mul and Photonis Germany (formerly ProxiVision), acquired by the Group in October 2023, July 2023 and June 2023, respectively, as well as Centronic and LR Tech, acquired by the Group in July 2024 and September 2024, respectively.
PR_FY24.events: Centronic (July 2024) and LR Tech (September 2024) acquired; NVLS agreement announced October 2024 (closing expected in the coming months); Noxant acquisition announced November 2024, set to close in Q1 2025.

PR_9M25.microwave_amplification_disposal_verbati: In line with its strategy to focus resources on higher-value activities which are closely aligned with its long-term priorities, the group has decided to divest its Microwave Amplification business. The signing of the asset purchase agreement marks a key step in this process, with the transaction expected to close latest in early 2026. In 2024, the group's Microwave Amplification business generated €10.6 million in revenue and a €1.3 million adjusted EBITDA loss, and consumed €5 million in cash. While the divestment will not generate cash inflows, the group expects to recognize a non-cash accounting loss in 2025, reflecting the impairment of goodwill and associated assets. Overall, the transaction will have a positive impact on the Group's profitability and cash profile once completed.
orders_and_capacity: Exosens has decided to further expand capacity by +15% with an additional €17 million investment in Europe. In total, this decision brings the 2025 announced investments to €37 million, which are expected to deliver a combined +40% increase in the group's global capacity by 2027, covering the 18mm, 16mm and 5G product families.
The group has received orders for over 5,000 5G tubes prior to the product's official launch, already making 5G a commercial success.

On 29 September 2025, Exosens announced that it has secured a major contract with the Spanish army for the supply of 17,000 advanced night vision monoculars from NVLS, utilizing its 16mm 4G intensifier tubes, to be delivered between 2025 and 2028.
Closing of Phasics (October 2025), a leader in wave front sensing technologies; closed on 20 October 2025.
PR_9M25.outlook_verbatim: Exosens expects a continued strong performance in 2025, with revenue growth in the high-teens and adjusted EBITDA growth in the low twenties compared to 2024 [footnote: Following the divestment of the group's Microwave Amplification ("MA") business, 2024 revenue and adjusted EBITDA have been restated in accordance with IFRS 5. Accordingly, the group generated revenue of €383.4 million and adjusted EBITDA of €119.8 million in 2024 on a restated basis (excluding MA business).] The Group expects high-teens 2024-2026 adjusted EBITDA CAGR and a cash conversion ratio in the range of 70%-75% over the period, taking into account capacity investment in Europe and in the US. Furthermore, the Group intends to pursue its selective external growth strategy, at a pace consistent with historical trend, while maintaining a leverage ratio of around 2x.
PR_9M25.like_for_like_definition: Like-for-like growth for the nine-month period ended 30 September 2025 therefore excludes the contribution of Centronic and LR Tech, acquired by the Group in July 2024 and September 2024, respectively, as well as Noxant and NVLS, acquired by the Group in March 2025 and July 2025, respectively.

PR_FY25.outlook_2026_verbatim: Exosens expects to deliver a solid performance in 2026, driven by continued commercial momentum, particularly in the Defense and Surveillance markets, as well as its operational excellence, and has set the following objectives: Revenue in the range of €520 million to €540 million; Adjusted EBITDA in the range of €168 million to €178 million. In addition, the Group intends to continue implementing its investment plan aimed at expanding production capacity by 40% by 2027, both in Europe and the United States, to meet strong demand, while continuing its efforts to improve productivity. In this context, the Group expects capital expenditure to represent around 9% of 2026 revenue (excluding capitalized R&D expenses, expected at around 3% of revenue).
PR_FY25.mid_term_outlook_verbatim: In this context, the Group targets medium-term average annual organic revenue growth up to mid-teens [footnote 9: Versus previously above mid-single digit yearly growth over the period 2025–2027]. In addition, the Group targets medium-term average annual organic adjusted EBITDA growth above 15% [footnote 10: Versus previously high single-digit average annual growth over the period 2025–2027], implying a mild progressive improvement in the adjusted EBITDA margin. Moreover, in response to accelerating global demand, the Group will continue to actively assess staggered capacity expansions to capture additional revenue growth. After completion of the current capacity expansion by 2027, Exosens expects normalized capital expenditure to represent around 5% of revenue (excluding capitalized R&D expenses, expected at around 3% of revenue).
PR_FY25.capital_allocation_verbatim: With regard to external growth, Exosens intends to pursue its strategy of targeted, value-creating acquisitions across its existing markets, focused on technology, with the ambition of reaching €1 billion in revenue. In light of this strategy, the Group's net financial debt to adjusted EBITDA ratio may temporarily increase over the period, reaching around 2x. Finally, the Group intends to continue its shareholder return policy, with an annual dividend payout ratio ranging between 20% and 25% of net income.
orders_and_capacity: Most notably, in late 2025, Exosens announced the signing of an unprecedented contract, in partnership with Theon International, with OCCAR [Organization for Joint Armament Cooperation] to supply the German armed-forces. This contract embeds 200,000 16mm tubes, for a total value of more than €500 million, for deliveries from 2027 to 2029.

Exosens announced in 2025 a €37 million investment plan to expand production capacity in both Europe and the U.S., targeting a 40% increase by 2027 across the 16mm, 18mm and 5G product families. ... in the U.S., where the rollout of the new manufacturing facility is underway, with key equipment already ordered and initial personnel hires completed.

The 5G has already seen rapid market adoption, resulting in sizeable orders, as illustrated by the signing in January 2026 of a major contract with ACTinBlack for the supply of more than 7,000 5G tubes, to be delivered across 2027 and 2028 and integrated into night vision goggles for European special forces end users.

Exosens announced a major contract with the Spanish army for the supply of 17,000 advanced night vision monoculars by NVLS, incorporating its 16mm 4G intensifier tubes, with deliveries scheduled between 2025 and 2028.
PR_FY25.microwave_amplification_disposal_verbati: Moreover, in line with its strategy to focus resources on higher-value activities closely aligned with its long-term priorities, the Group decided to divest its Microwave Amplifier business. The transaction was completed on 31 December 2025 and is expected to have a positive impact on Exosens' profitability and cash generation profile. ... Net loss from continued operations amounted to €27.5 million in 2025 compared with €3.4 million in 2024, reflecting the net loss recognized on the sale of Microwave Amplifier assets, primarily non-cash. [sic: the release text says 'Net loss from continued operations' where the table line is 'Profit / (loss) from discontinued activities'.]
PR_FY25.like_for_like_definition: Like-for-like growth for the full-year ended 31 December 2025 therefore excludes the contribution of Centronic and LR Tech, acquired by the Group in July 2024 and September 2024, respectively, as well as Noxant, NVLS and Phasics, acquired by the Group in March 2025, July 2025 and October 2025, respectively.

PR_Q126.title: Exosens delivers strong Q1 2026 performance, with accelerating defense momentum in digital imaging and night vision; fully on track to deliver on 2026 guidance
PR_Q126.basis_note: Q1 2025 comparatives are the restated (ex-Microwave Amplification, IFRS 5) figures (Q1 2025 total 102.4, Amplification 79.1); no restatement footnote is printed in this release. Q1 2026 excludes Emberion (closed 24 April 2026).

revenue_growth_pct.text_note: Amplification 72% of Group sales, D&I 28%. Group LFL printed +12.0% here but +12.5% for Q1 2026 in the PR_H126 / PR_9M26 appendices.

adjusted_gross_margin_by_segment.mix_note_verbatim: The first-quarter 2026 adjusted gross margin rate was in line with the Group's expectations. However, the mix by segment is not fully representative of the expected full-year profile and should progressively normalize. This reflects (i) in Amplification, the timing of NVLS' product deliveries, with revenue expected to ramp up over the remainder of the year following its limited contribution in the first quarter, and (ii) in D&I, a stronger contribution from higher-margin detectors and cameras.

PR_Q126.outlook_verbatim: Exosens expects to deliver a solid performance in 2026, driven by continued commercial momentum, particularly in the defense and surveillance end markets, as well as operational excellence, and has set the following objectives: Revenue in the range of €520 million to €540 million; Adjusted EBITDA in the range of €168 million to €178 million. In addition, the Group intends to continue implementing its investment plan aimed at expanding production capacity by 40% by 2027, both in Europe and the United States, to meet strong demand, while continuing its efforts to improve productivity. In this context, the Group expects capital expenditure to represent around 9% of 2026 revenue (excluding capitalized R&D expenses, expected at around 3% of revenue).
orders_and_capacity: Underscoring the effectiveness of its industrial strategy in the U.S., the Group reached a key milestone with the award in February 2026 of a firm-fixed-price Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract by the U.S. Army for the development, production, and testing of the Binocular Night Observation Device (BiNOD). (No contract value printed in this release.)

Exosens announced in 2025 an investment plan to expand production capacity in Europe and the U.S., targeting a 40% increase by 2027 ... The plan is progressing as expected, with the initial benefits from capacity expansion in Europe expected from the second half of 2026.

Exosens secured a record order for interceptor drone-based digital imaging solutions from a major European air defense systems developer. Following this milestone, total orders secured over the past two quarters exceed 10,000 cameras across air, land, and sea unmanned platforms.

On 24 April 2026, Exosens completed the acquisition of Emberion, a Finland- and UK-based company specializing in ... quantum dot imaging technology ... The company generated revenue of approximately €0.7 million in the 2025 fiscal year.
PR_Q126.like_for_like_definition: Like-for-like growth for the three-month period ended 31 March 2026 therefore excludes the contribution of Noxant, NVLS and Phasics, which were acquired by the Group in March 2025, July 2025 and October 2025, respectively.

PR_H126.outlook_verbatim: Building on sustained commercial momentum, particularly in the Defense and Surveillance markets, and strong operational execution, Exosens remains fully on track to deliver on its 2026 guidance and now expects revenue and adjusted EBITDA to be towards the upper end of their respective ranges: Revenue in the range of €520 million to €540 million; Adjusted EBITDA in the range of €168 million to €178 million. In addition, the Group intends to continue implementing its investment plan aimed at expanding production capacity by 40% by 2027, both in Europe and the United States, to meet strong demand, while continuing its efforts to improve productivity. In this context, the Group expects capital expenditure to represent around 9% of 2026 revenue (excluding capitalized R&D expenses, expected at around 3% of revenue).

outlook_2026.qualifier: towards the upper end of their respective ranges

orders_and_capacity: Exosens reached a key milestone with the award of a major IDIQ U.S. Army contract for the development, production and testing of Binocular Night Observation Device (BiNOD). (No value printed in this release.)

Commercial momentum remained particularly strong in Europe, supported by the continued execution of major night vision procurement programs, including the OCCAR framework for the German and Belgian armed forces.

Exosens announced in 2025 an investment plan to expand its production capacity in Europe and the U.S., targeting a 40% increase by 2027. The plan is progressing on schedule, with the first benefits from the European capacity expansion expected from H2 2026. ... Exosens is actively evaluating further capacity additions.
The Group secured a record order for interceptor drone-based imaging solutions from a major European air defense systems developer.
To support this accelerating demand, the Group is doubling its production capacity for cooled infrared cameras in 2026.

Extension of its Revolving Credit Facility (RCF) from €100 million to €200 million, with improved financial terms, and ... a new €140 million financing facility with the European Investment Bank (EIB).
PR_H126.like_for_like_definition: Accordingly, like-for-like growth for the six-month period ended 30 June 2026 excludes the contribution of Noxant, NVLS and Phasics, which were acquired by the Group in March 2025, July 2025 and October 2025, respectively.
PR_H126.events: Emberion acquisition completed 24 April 2026; trademark impairment of €(28.2) million recognized in connection with rebranding under the single Exosens brand.

PR_9M26.title: Exosens delivers +23.5% revenue growth in Q3 2026, driven by stronger demand and faster-than-expected capacity ramp-up; fully on track to meet upgraded 2026 outlook
PR_9M26.basis_note: 9M 2025 comparatives are the restated (ex-Microwave Amplification, IFRS 5) figures as printed in PR_9M25 / PR_FY25; no restatement footnote is printed in this release. 9M 2026 includes Emberion from 24 April 2026.

revenue_growth_pct.text_note: Q3 2026 total growth +23.5% incl. +20.5% LFL (vs +11.4% LFL in H1); Amplification growth accelerated to +23.9% in Q3 2026 from +11.6% in H1 2026. Amplification c.69% of Group sales, D&I c.31%.

adjusted_gross_margin_by_segment.text_note: Q3 2025 Amplification margin rate reached 54.9%, versus 50.5% for full-year 2025 (high comparison base). Margin pressure from NVLS complete-system deliveries ramping in Q3 2026 and staffing costs at the U.S. facility.

PR_9M26.outlook_verbatim: Building on sustained commercial momentum, reflected in the clear acceleration in like-for-like revenue growth in the third quarter, as well as continued disciplined execution, Exosens confirms its upgraded full-year 2026 guidance announced on 17 September 2026. The Group expects: Revenue in the range of €558 million to €570 million; Adjusted EBITDA in the range of €186 million to €192 million; Capital expenditure at around 9% of revenue (excluding capitalized R&D expenses of around 3% of revenue), driven by production capacity expansion in Europe and the U.S. Exosens will communicate its full-year 2027 guidance upon publication of the Group's full-year 2026 results on 22 February 2027.

outlook_2026.headline: c.20% revenue growth and c.25% adjusted EBITDA growth at midpoint vs. 2025

orders_and_capacity: Exosens reached a key milestone in August 2026 when its U.S. subsidiary, Photonis Defense, was awarded a first delivery order for 1,600 complete systems under the U.S. Army's Binocular Night Observation Device (BiNOD) program, as part of the broader US$352.6 million Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract announced in March 2026. The order marks the transition from key testing and qualification to the Low-Rate Initial Production (LRIP) phase ... First product deliveries are expected by the end of 2026, with the bulk of deliveries scheduled throughout 2027.
Demand continued to exceed available production capacity in 9M 2026. ... notably under major night vision procurement programs such as the OCCAR framework for the German and Belgian armed forces.

Exosens continues to implement its investment plan to expand production capacity across Europe and the United States by 40% by 2027. The first phase in Europe was successfully implemented, with an extended operating schedule enabling production to run throughout August for the first time, while newly installed production equipment was commissioned. As a result, additional European production capacity ramped up faster than expected.
To meet growing demand, Exosens is implementing plans to triple production capacity for thermal cameras and double capacity for cooled infrared cameras in 2026.

Exosens supplied advanced neutron flux monitoring detectors and related technical expertise to Antares Nuclear and Valar Atomics, the developers behind the first two reactor designs to reach criticality under the [DOE Reactor Pilot] program.
PR_9M26.like_for_like_definition: Accordingly, like-for-like growth for the nine-month period ended 30 September 2026 excludes the contributions of Noxant, NVLS, Phasics and Emberion, which were acquired by the Group in March 2025, July 2025, October 2025 and April 2026, respectively.

PR_OUTLOOK_20260917.title: Exosens raises full-year 2026 guidance, driven by faster-than-expected capacity ramp-up and strong commercial momentum
PR_OUTLOOK_20260917.outlook_verbatim: Against this backdrop, Exosens is raising its full-year 2026 guidance and now expects: Revenue in the range of €558 million to €570 million (compared with €520 million to €540 million previously); Adjusted EBITDA in the range of €186 million to €192 million (compared with €168 million to €178 million previously); Capital expenditure at around 9% of revenue (excluding capitalized R&D expenses of around 3% of revenue), driven by production capacity expansion in Europe and the U.S. (unchanged). ... 2026 guidance raised: c.20% revenue growth and c.25% adjusted EBITDA growth at midpoint vs. 2025, implying further profitability improvement. Exosens will communicate its full-year 2027 guidance upon publication of the Group's full-year 2026 results on 22 February 2027.
PR_OUTLOOK_20260917.capacity_verbatim: In Amplification, Exosens maintained production throughout August at its European facilities for the first time, with the extended operating schedule implemented as planned. Newly installed production equipment was also successfully commissioned. These operational milestones have confirmed the faster-than-expected ramp-up of additional capacity for high-performance image intensifier tubes in Europe. ... In Detection & Imaging ... the Group is scaling its industrial capabilities, with plans to triple production capacity for thermal cameras and double capacity for cooled infrared cameras in 2026.
